name: Bhavesh Joshi
summary: The paper-bag vigilante of Vikramaditya Motwane's 2018 Hindi film Bhavesh Joshi Superhero. A grounded, gritty take on the Indian masked hero set in Mumbai.
origin: Bhavesh Joshi comes from a 2018 vigilante film in which three friends meet at an anti-corruption rally and start a YouTube show, Insaaf TV. After Bhavesh is killed, his friend Siku takes up the mask and name to fight a water-siphoning scheme. Vikramaditya Motwane directed.
creators: Vikas Bahl, Madhu Mantena and Anurag Kashyap (producers)
powers: DIY mask with LED eye lights
Online reach through the Insaaf TV channel

storyline.title: Three friends and a rally
storyline.beat: Three friends meet at an anti-corruption rally and run a YouTube show, Insaaf TV, exposing local corruption.

storyline.title: A vigilante falls
storyline.beat: Bhavesh grows obsessive about vigilantism and is killed by the water-mafia boss Patil.

storyline.title: Siku steps in
storyline.beat: Siku, who blames himself, secretly takes up the mask and Bhavesh's identity to fight a water scheme backed by a minister.

storyline.title: Streaming and cult following
storyline.beat: A box-office bomb in theatres, it reaches Netflix on 16 August 2018. Wikipedia credits its later cult following to the societal relevance of its themes.

gossip.text: Early masks were paper bags with painted faces, which the film's own heroes call DIY.
Imran Khan was first considered for the lead, then Sidharth Malhotra, before Harshvardhan Kapoor got the role after delays.
The film cost about Rs 21 crore and earned only about Rs 2.52 crore.
The name Insaaf-Man was invented by the character Rajat.
Nishikant Kamat, who plays the villain minister Rana, made his last screen appearance in this film.

quiz.why: The friends run Insaaf TV to expose corruption.

theme.tagline: Rain, graffiti and a homemade mask.

timeline.title: Theme single arrives
timeline.note: The first song, Hum Hain Insaaf by Babu Haabi and Naezy, is released on 12 May 2018.

timeline.title: Soundtrack released
timeline.note: The full soundtrack, composed by Amit Trivedi, comes out on 23 May 2018.

timeline.title: Theatrical release
timeline.note: It opens in India on 1 June 2018 and flops against a Rs 21 crore budget.

timeline.title: Netflix premiere
timeline.note: It arrives on Netflix on 16 August 2018, after a weak run in cinemas.

facts.text: Imran Khan was first picked for the lead, then Sidharth Malhotra. Wikipedia says Malhotra was replaced by Harshvardhan Kapoor because of frequent delays in the film's pre-production.
It cost about Rs 21 crore and earned only about Rs 2.52 crore, making it a box-office bomb.
The heroes begin as YouTube hosts, and they wear paper bags with frown faces drawn on them while pulling off small vigilante stunts.
The villains fit extra pipes to city water mains to siphon free water into tankers, then sell it back to the residents who were already entitled to it.
In the early days their crusades are tiny: stopping public urination and chopping down a roadside tree, with videos that get only hundreds of views.
After Bhavesh is gone, Siku fakes a trip to the US and hides in an abandoned hotel that was once the gang's safe house.
Siku presents himself on Insaaf TV as the supposedly still-alive Bhavesh Joshi, so he borrows his friend's name along with the mask.
Siku trains in karate and eskrima, a Filipino stick-fighting art, and gets a motorcycle fitted with nitro cylinders.
The villain minister Rana compares Siku to Icarus, who flew too close to the sun, and casts himself as the sun.
The rap anthem Hum Hain Insaaf was co-sung by Naezy, the Mumbai rapper whose life helped inspire the film Gully Boy.

The villains blow up the city's water pipes to cause a drinking-water crisis. Then the minister Rana offers the Chief Minister free water in return for control of future water contracts, and both become popular.
When Rajat accuses Siku of wanting to be a comic-book hero, Siku answers that he does not want to be a hero at all, only to stop Bhavesh's work from having been for nothing.
In 2016 Harshvardhan Kapoor told PTI the film was not a superhero film, and said he did not know where reports of a Gujarati boy with special powers had come from.
Harshvardhan said he and Motwane first discussed the film in 2012. Before shooting he did a workshop from 1 July, asked for two more weeks, and moved in with the actor playing his roommate.
The posters were styled like graphic-novel pages, showing the masked silhouette rather than the star, as Motwane said Batman and Superman posters sell the character, not the actor.
The poster look drew on Mumbai's wall graffiti and anime, with lots of primary colours. Seek Red's Sucharita Sengupta Suri designed them, starting about a year before release.
Posters highlighted the DIY mask with LED lights around the eyes, because the mask plays an important role in the film.
The story starts during the India Against Corruption movement, and DailyO says the film draws its moral drive from the failures of the Anna Hazare-led campaign.
DailyO notes the film name-checks earlier Indian hero films such as Krrish, Ra.One, Flying Jatt and Shahenshah, and calls it the most realistic vigilante film made in India so far.
DailyO's writer spotted Easter eggs in the visuals, homages to Chinatown, The Dark Knight and, in a way, the whole body of Frank Miller's comic work.

kidSummary: Bhavesh and Siku film a YouTube show where they put on paper-bag masks and catch small-time cheats. When their friend Bhavesh is lost fighting a gang that steals the city's water, Siku puts on the mask himself and keeps up the fight as Insaaf-Man. Note: this is a film for older viewers, with violence, not a children's film.

story.title: Paper-bag heroes
story.text: Bhavesh, Siku and Rajat become friends and start Insaaf TV, a YouTube show about local wrongdoing.

story.title: The water scheme
story.text: Bhavesh discovers a gang that siphons the city's free water into tankers and sells it back to residents.

story.title: A friend lost
story.text: Bhavesh is lost fighting the gang, and Siku blames himself.

story.title: Siku wears the mask
story.text: Siku hides, trains hard and takes up the mask, even using Bhavesh's name to keep the fight alive.

story.title: Insaaf-Man
story.text: In the end he fights as himself under the name Rajat invented: Insaaf-Man.
